rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(total orthopaedic solutions|surgical navigation)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 is the main NHS Supply Chain route for this patch and carries 101 named suppliers, but being named on it is evidence of a route, not of volume, and NHS Supply Chain is only one route. The award record below shows orthopaedic and trauma implants bought through NHS Wales Shared Services, National Procurement in Scotland, the Business Services Organisation in Northern Ireland and trusts' own direct awards, none of which appears in the framework list above. Surgical Navigation Systems is shared with neurosurgery and ENT. No unit or market-share split is published for any of it, and none is claimed here.
rules.suppliers: Every supplier NHS Supply Chain names on the frameworks above, resolved to one name per company through the Hub's alias registry, and ordered by how many of this speciality's frameworks they appear on. That count is the only claim made. It is not a ranking of size or share. Where NHS Supply Chain spelled a company two ways across its own pages, both spellings are shown against the one entry. COVERAGE LIMIT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 is the main NHS Supply Chain route for this patch and carries 101 named suppliers, but being named on it is evidence of a route, not of volume, and NHS Supply Chain is only one route. The award record below shows orthopaedic and trauma implants bought through NHS Wales Shared Services, National Procurement in Scotland, the Business Services Organisation in Northern Ireland and trusts' own direct awards, none of which appears in the framework list above. Surgical Navigation Systems is shared with neurosurgery and ENT. No unit or market-share split is published for any of it, and none is claimed here.
rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(orthopaedic\w*|orthopedic\w*|orthobiologic\w*|trauma\w*|tos3|arthroplast\w*|joint replacement|hip\b|knee\b|shoulder\b|elbow\b|ankle\b|spinal|spine\b|scoliosis|vertebr\w*|pedicle|interbody|kyphoplast\w*|vertebroplast\w*|discectom\w*|laminectom\w*|fractur\w*|osteotom\w*|osteosynthes\w*|femur|acetabul\w*|bone (?:cement|graft|substitute|prep|screw|anchor|plate|mill|void filler)|arthroscop\w*|cruciate|meniscal|meniscus|external fixation|fixator|intramedullary|tourniquet\w*|sagittal saw|pulse lavage|musculoskelet\w*|limb reconstruction)\b/i and does not match /\b(medicines|spinal cord stimulat\w*|epidural|fgm|sexual abuse|spinal muscular atrophy|orthotic\w*|orthos[ei]s|manikins?|mannequins?|simulat\w*)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 331417 or 33183 or 85121283 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: No Drug Tariff part applies to this speciality. Part IX reimburses dressings and elastic hosiery (IXA), incontinence appliances (IXB), stoma appliances (IXC) and elastic hosiery (IXR); nothing on this patch is listed there, so the panel carries no tariff rather than reaching for the nearest part.
rules.directorySuppliers: Companies the Hub's own supplier directory files under this speciality, from the speciality labels on each company's directory record, resolved through speciality-label-map.json and speciality-map.json (Compare ids: ortho). They are labelled DIRECTORY-TAGGED because the tag is the Hub's filing of a company's range, not a procurement record: being listed here is not evidence of a contract or of volume, and the list is not a census of the market. A company that is also on this speciality's own frameworks is listed once, with the framework-named suppliers, and marked as also directory-tagged. WHERE A COMPANY IS ON ANOTHER FRAMEWORK: where a directory-tagged company is named on an NHS Supply Chain framework that is not counted as this speciality's, it is still listed, with that framework named against it and linked, so it is not lost from the page. 4 of the 6 listed here carry such a note. Framework names and links come from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs as held in frameworks.json; an agreement the directory records from another buying organisation, such as an NHS Shared Business Services framework, is shown as the directory states it.
rules.gpPrescribing: No BNF section is mapped to this speciality, so no GP prescribing market is sized here rather than borrowing a neighbouring page's.
rules.mhraDsu: Every MHRA Drug Safety Update that GOV.UK itself tags to a therapeutic area mapped to this speciality in config/mhra-dsu-speciality-map.json. The speciality comes only from GOV.UK's own facet, never from the title or the text. The monthly 'Letters and medicine recalls sent to healthcare professionals' roundup is left out (0 here), and so is any update GOV.UK ticks against 30 or more therapeutic areas, which is a message to everyone rather than to this speciality (2 here). Newest first; the count is every tagged update in the archive, and the list shows the most recent. MHRA Drug Safety Update, GOV.UK, as at 2026-10-03.

localIntel.title: Musculoskeletal elective treatment waiting times and labour market outcomes, England: 2014 to 2025
localIntel.fact: Among working-age NHS patients having elective inpatient treatment for musculoskeletal (MSK) pain in England between April 2015 and March 2023, each extra four weeks of waiting reduced annual earnings by up to £487 (other joint disorders), £392 (other MSK conditions), £329 (back, neck and MSK pain) and £301 (osteoarthritis). ONS found no statistical evidence of a link between waiting time and later employment status or benefit receipt.
localIntel.quote: each additional four weeks of waiting led to a £487 reduction in annual earnings in the fourth year after treatment
localIntel.use: A cost-of-waiting figure for elective orthopaedic recovery and theatre throughput conversations.

localIntel.title: Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 (TOS3): the national route for orthopaedic, trauma and spine
localIntel.fact: Reference 2023/S 000-025037, 48 months from 1 February 2024, ending 30 January 2028, with no option to extend. Three lots: Lot 1 Implants and Consumables (12 sub-lots: 1.1 Hip, 1.2 Knee, 1.3 Extremities, 1.4 Complex Arthroplasty, 1.5 Internal and External Fixation, 1.6 Spine, 1.7 Arthroscopy and Fluid Management, 1.8 Bone Preparation, 1.9 Power Tool Consumables, 1.10 Regenerative Technology, 1.11 Orthopaedic Additional Devices, 1.12 Custom and Customisable Implants); Lot 2 Equipment (robotics, navigation, imaging and others); Lot 3 Services and Solutions. NHS Supply Chain's own page lists 101 awarded suppliers (21 marked New) and 5 delisted.
localIntel.quote: There is no option to extend.
localIntel.use: Robotics and navigation sit in Lot 2, so they are bought through this framework. The end date is 30 January 2028 and the successor (TOS4) is already in the pipeline.

localIntel.title: Total Orthopaedic Solutions 4 (TOS4): preliminary market engagement notice for the TOS3 successor
localIntel.fact: Notice 2026/S 000-081660 is a UK2 preliminary market engagement notice, not an award. Estimated value £3,000,000,000 excluding VAT (£3,600,000,000 including). Scope: orthopaedic, trauma and spine devices, equipment management services and orthopaedic services. The planned tender publication date moved from 7 October 2026 to 19 October 2026 in the 27 August 2026 edit, and bone reconstruction cements (CPV 33697110) was added. The engagement deadline was 30 September 2026. Requirements stated for future tenders include ISO 9001:2015 or ISO 13485:2016 (or Medical Device Single Audit Program) certification, a Modern Slavery Assessment Tool score of 41% or above, Evergreen Level 1 and, where patient data or IT is handled, Cyber Essentials Plus.
localIntel.quote: The planned publication date has changed from 7th October 2026 to 19th October 2026.
localIntel.use: The tender that decides who sits on the national orthopaedic route from February 2028. Check the Find a Tender notice for the tender itself from 19 October 2026.

localIntel.title: Surgical Navigation Systems with Associated Options and Related Services
localIntel.fact: Reference 2021/S 000-007768, 72 months from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2028 (an initial 24-month extension followed by a further 24-month extension). Product categories: Cranial Neurosurgery/Spinal Surgery, ENT, and Orthopaedic/Trauma Surgical Navigation Systems. Six suppliers are named on the page: Brainlab, Hospital Services Limited, Karl Storz Endoscopy (UK), Medtronic, Stryker UK and T.J.Smith and Nephew. The page states no supplier count and no lot split by supplier.
localIntel.quote: Surgical Navigation Systems are used to guide the surgeon’s movements during an operation.
localIntel.use: A second route for navigation, alongside TOS3 Lot 2. It ends on 31 March 2028, about two months after TOS3.

localIntel.title: TOS3 call-offs by trusts, with end dates beyond the framework's own
localIntel.fact: Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust awarded 'KGH Lot 1.5 Trauma Implants Medartis' (£10,872) and Northampton General Hospital NHS Trust awarded 'NGH Lot 1.5 Trauma Implants Medartis' (£68,072), both published 2 July 2026 as call-offs from a framework agreement, running 22 April 2026 to 21 April 2030, with NHS Supply Chain Coordination Limited as the named supplier. An earlier Northampton notice of 1 July 2026 (£152,000 to £56,000) was replaced the next day. Oxford University Hospitals published 'NHSSC - TOS3 1.8a Bone Prep Award' on 24 June 2026: Zimmer Biomet UK Limited, £132,638.46, 15 May 2026 to 31 January 2028, described as non-commitment.
localIntel.quote: Award of lot 1.8a Bone Prep to Zimmer Biomet - non commitment.
localIntel.use: Shows how trusts actually call off TOS3 by sub-lot. The Northamptonshire contracts run to April 2030, past TOS3's end date of 30 January 2028, so a call-off does not end with the framework.

localIntel.title: Purchase of Orthopaedic Trauma & Extremity Implants & Consumables
localIntel.ends: 36 months from award, two optional extensions
localIntel.fact: Contract notice 2025/S 000-028366 (29 May 2025) set 21 lots and an estimated £340,000,000 excluding VAT for 36 months with renewal options. Named suppliers per lot include 17 on Bone Graft & Biomaterials, 17 on Foot & Ankle, 16 on Shoulder & Clavicle, 9 on Universal Pins, Screws & Plates and 3 each on ceiling-price lots such as the short and long cephalomedullary nails, the dynamic hip screw and the standard tibial nail.
localIntel.quote: Purchase of Orthopaedic Trauma & Extremity Implants & Consumables

localIntel.title: All Wales Orthopaedic, Trauma and Joint Replacement Framework
localIntel.ends: 31/01/2026 per the May 2025 notice; later status not verified
localIntel.fact: Modification notice 2025/S 000-027654, published 27 May 2025, lists 61 suppliers and a total value of £141,950,000 excluding VAT. Ten lots: Primary and Revision Hip; Primary and Revision Knee; Extremities Arthroplasty; Trauma/Maxillofacial; Spinal; Arthroscopy Products; Bone Preparation; Orthopaedic Power Tools and Consumables; Biologics; Value-Based Procurement & Innovation. It started 1 August 2021 and NWSSP extended it to 31 January 2026 'to facilitate a redesign of approach to market'. A February 2026 Cardiff and Vale award still refers to the All Wales Framework. What replaced it after 31 January 2026 is not verified: no later framework notice was found in this check.
localIntel.quote: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership intends to extend the current agreement until 31st January 2026.
localIntel.use: Wales had a ten-lot national framework with 61 suppliers. Its successor route is not verified, so ask NWSSP before assuming one.

localIntel.org: Cardiff and Vale University Health Board (via NWSSP)
localIntel.title: Cardiff and Vale Knee Contract: four-year sole supply commitment to Zimmer Biomet
localIntel.fact: Contract award notice 2026/S 000-021902, published 11 March 2026, contract concluded 20 February 2026. Cardiff and Vale University Health Board entered a four-year sole supply commitment for knee implants with Zimmer Biomet UK Limited, covering approximately 80% of knee procedures via the All Wales Framework, valued at £3,384,842 excluding VAT. One tender was received.
localIntel.quote: four-year sole supply commitment for knee implants with Zimmer Biomet
localIntel.use: An example of a Welsh health board committing about 80% of knee volume to one supplier through the national framework.

localIntel.org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
localIntel.title: HTG743: Robot-assisted surgery for orthopaedic procedures, early value assessment
localIntel.fact: Six technologies can be used in the NHS during the evidence generation period as options for robot-assisted knee or hip replacement: ApolloKnee, CORI, Mako SmartRobotics, ROSA Knee, SkyWalker and VELYS. Use is conditional on evidence being generated under NICE's evidence generation plan and on regulatory approval including NHS England's Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC) approval. The evidence generation period is 3 years, after which NICE will assess whether routine adoption is appropriate. NICE has renumbered the content from Health technology evaluation 22 to HealthTech guidance 743, unchanged.
localIntel.quote: Six technologies can be used in the NHS during the evidence generation period as options for robot-assisted surgery for knee or hip replacements.
localIntel.use: Robot-assisted knee and hip surgery is allowed only while evidence is generated. A rep selling a robot needs to know the evidence plan commitments.

localIntel.org: Getting It Right First Time (GIRFT) and British Orthopaedic Association (BOA)
localIntel.title: Five high-volume, low-complexity (HVLC) orthopaedic pathways updated
localIntel.fact: GIRFT updated five national elective pathways with the BOA and specialist societies: total primary hip replacement; total and unicompartmental primary knee replacement; Dupuytren's disease; shoulder arthroscopy for rotator cuff repair or subacromial decompression; hallux valgus and rigidus. First issued in 2020. The 2026 updates align the follow-up sections with GIRFT's Further Faster Follow-Up Protocols and Standardising Follow-Up guidance. A joint GIRFT and BOA webinar is on 13 October 2026, 1pm to 2pm.
localIntel.quote: it is imperative that all teams across England adopt them
localIntel.use: The pathways set how clinics and theatres are run for the five highest-volume elective procedures, which shapes what trusts buy and when.

localIntel.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
localIntel.title: MHRA orthopaedic Device Safety Information (DSI) since 2024
localIntel.fact: GOV.UK's Device Safety Information list tagged Orthopaedics returns these implant items: DSI/2026/010 Cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements (26 August 2026); DSI/2026/001 M6-C Artificial Cervical Disc, Spinal Kinetics, new monitoring for osteolysis (15 January 2026); DSI/2025/005 Profemur cobalt chrome modular neck hip replacements (4 September 2025); DSI/2024/007 CPT Hip System femoral stem 12/14 neck taper, periprosthetic femoral fracture (4 September 2024); DSI/2024/005 Symbios ORIGIN posterior stabilised patient-matched total knee, early revision (23 April 2024); DSI/2024/002 MAGEC X System, UK suspension lifted (12 March 2024). The same list holds one non-implant item, DSI/2026/003 on blood transfusion giving sets.
localIntel.quote: Cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements: risk of metal-wear effects and revision surgery (DSI/2026/010)
localIntel.use: A standing list of recent implant safety actions a rep can be asked about at any trust.

localIntel.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
localIntel.title: DSI/2026/010: cobalt-chrome modular neck hip replacements, all withdrawn before 2019
localIntel.fact: An MHRA investigation of every hip replacement with a cobalt-chrome modular neck ever sold in the UK found increased wear and corrosion risk and a possible increase in revision for adverse local tissue reaction. All of these devices were removed from the market before 2019 and none remain commercially available. MHRA advises trusts to use the National Joint Registry (NJR) and local records to identify patients and invite them for virtual or face-to-face review; symptomatic patients annually, asymptomatic patients on a patient-initiated follow-up pathway. Table 1 (NJR data extracted June 2026) covers Aesculap Metha modular, LimaCorporate H-Max-M, Smith and Nephew SMF, Stryker ABG II modular and Symbios HARMONY modular and SPS modular. The advice for distributors is that there is none.
localIntel.quote: there is no advice for distributors regarding this DSI
localIntel.use: This is a patient-recall workload for trusts, not a product-switching event: the devices are off the market and distributors have no action. Do not frame it as a competitor opening.

localIntel.title: NJR 23rd Annual Report 2026: hips, knees and robotic use (surgical data to 31 December 2025)
localIntel.fact: Primary hip replacements using unipolar implants reached 113,472 in 2025, a record for the fourth year running. Primary knee replacements reached a record 143,972 in 2025; NHS-funded procedures in NHS facilities have plateaued and now represent less than 50% of knee volume, against over 60% historically. Robotic procedures recorded in 2025: 3,762 hip and 11,641 knee. Mako was the most-used knee system (7,869) followed by CORI (1,590); CORI use roughly doubled since 2023; VELYS had its first recorded use in 2024; six knee systems have data recorded. Robotic hip replacement rose from 2,854 in 2023 to 3,762 in 2025.
localIntel.quote: ANNUAL REPORT 2026
localIntel.use: Current national volumes and the robotics share for sizing a hip or knee patch. The NJR does not publish a market-size value.

localIntel.title: Referral to Treatment (RTT) waiting times: Trauma and Orthopaedic Service (C_110) by trust
localIntel.fact: NHS England publishes monthly RTT provider files by treatment function; the latest on the 2026-27 page is July 2026. In the July 2026 full extract, Trauma and Orthopaedic Service is treatment function code C_110, with rows for completed admitted and non-admitted pathways, incomplete pathways, incomplete pathways with a decision to admit, and new RTT periods, at provider and commissioner level. This entry gives the source only; it states no waiting-list total.
localIntel.quote: Incomplete pathways are waiting times for cases where patients are still waiting to start treatment at the end of the month.
localIntel.use: The standing source for trust-level orthopaedic waiting pressure. Pull the C_110 rows for a named trust before quoting any figure.

localIntel.title: GIRFT Orthopaedic Surgery workstream: reports, pathways and news
localIntel.fact: GIRFT's Orthopaedic Surgery page describes two published reports (2015 and a February 2020 follow-up) and names Professor Tim Briggs as clinical lead. The 2020 follow-up headline findings include a reduction in revision rates every year since 2012 and a 20% reduction in average length of stay, releasing more than 368,000 bed days. The site is behind a bot check, so scripts cannot read it, but a normal browser can.
localIntel.quote: A reduction in revision rates every year since 2012
localIntel.use: The entry point for GIRFT's orthopaedic pathways and news. Trust-level GIRFT data is not public.

localIntel.title: TOS3 Supplier Matrix by Lot (issued 24 March 2025): who can sell on each sub-lot
localIntel.fact: The matrix has 99 supplier rows. Suppliers marked per lot: 1.1 Hips 22; 1.2 Knees 21; 1.3 Extremities Arthroplasty 22; 1.4 Complex Arthroplasty 18; 1.5 Internal and External Fixation 32; 1.6 Spine 26; 1.7 Arthroscopy / Sports Medicine 20; 1.8 Bone Preparation 19; 1.9 Power Tools Consumables 20; 1.10 Regenerative Technology 30; 1.11 Orthopaedic Additional Devices 26; 1.12 Custom/Customisable Implants 20; Lot 2 Equipment 36; Lot 3 Services and Solutions 22. NHS Supply Chain's own TOS3 page lists 101 awarded supplier names, so the matrix (issued March 2025) and the page do not match; which two names are absent from the matrix is not established here.
localIntel.quote: Total Orthopaedic Solutions 3 - Supplier Matrix by Lot
localIntel.use: Shows how many competitors sit on each sub-lot, for example 32 on fixation against 18 on complex arthroplasty. Use the page, not this matrix, for the current supplier list.

localIntel.title: TOS3 Customer Engagement Guide: what Lots 2 and 3 cover
localIntel.fact: Lot 2 Equipment includes, but is not limited to: robotics, navigation, imaging, fluid management, consoles and arthroscopic stack systems, power tools, helmets (hoods/togas), tourniquet machines, bone harvesting/milling, ultrasound cement removal, cement mixing and ultrasound bone healing; consumables for equipment are in sub-lot 1.11. Lot 3 Services and Solutions includes, but is not limited to: wearable devices, patient/surgeon applications, software solutions, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) technology, efficiency programmes, patient planning, managed equipment services and technical support.
localIntel.quote: The consumables for equipment are found within sub lot 1.11.
localIntel.use: The authoritative list of what counts as equipment and services on TOS3. It is wider than the shorthand 'robotics, navigation, power tools'.

localIntel.title: TOS4 pipeline notice 2026/S 000-016123: the earlier notice, with a superseded tender date
localIntel.fact: The UK1 pipeline notice 'Musculoskeletal Surgical 2028 (Total Orthopaedic Solutions)', published 23 February 2026, shares its procurement identifier (ocds-h6vhtk-065a3d) with the UK2 engagement notice 2026/S 000-081660. It gave an estimated tender notice publication date of 1 November 2026, estimated value £3,000,000,000 excluding VAT, and contract dates 1 February 2028 to 31 January 2030 with a possible extension to 31 January 2032. The later notice moved the planned date to 19 October 2026. Any list still showing 1 November 2026, including the Hub's own NHS Supply Chain procurement calendar file, is using the older date.
localIntel.quote: Publication date of tender notice (estimated)
localIntel.use: Explains why two dates are in circulation. The 19 October 2026 date is the later one.

localIntel.title: SBS10238 Surgical Robots, Consumables and Related Services: a separate robotics route that names orthopaedics
localIntel.fact: Framework SBS10238 is active 24 May 2023 to 23 May 2027 and open to all NHS organisations in the UK. Its page lists orthopaedics among the specialties surgical robots serve (with urology, colorectal and gynaecology). It allows a further competition or direct award under Regulation 33 of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015. Three suppliers are named: CMR Surgical Limited, Intuitive Surgical Ltd and Medtronic. The page does not say which of them supply orthopaedic systems, so whether the framework is a route for hip or knee robots is not verified. TOS3 Lot 2 also lists robotics.
localIntel.quote: Via this framework agreement, you can run a further competition, or choose to direct award to a supplier
localIntel.use: A second robotics route exists outside TOS3. Check with SBS which of its three suppliers cover orthopaedic systems before telling a trust it is an option.

localIntel.title: Contracts Finder: where trust TOS3 call-offs are published
localIntel.fact: The Kettering, Northampton and Oxford TOS3 call-offs cited in this list were published on Contracts Finder as 'Call-off from a framework agreement' notices, each carrying contract start and end dates and a value. The search page accepts keywords across contract title, description and buyer. Search for 'TOS3' and for 'Lot 1.' (sub-lot numbers) to find further call-offs.
localIntel.quote: Can include contract title, description and buyer
localIntel.use: The place to find which trust has called off which TOS3 sub-lot, and when the call-off ends.

localIntel.org: Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)
localIntel.title: MHRA weekly Field Safety Notices page
localIntel.fact: MHRA publishes manufacturers' Field Safety Notices (FSNs) as one page a week. The latest at this check is 'Field Safety Notices: 21 to 25 September 2026', published 29 September 2026. Entries give manufacturer, product, date and MHRA reference and are not tagged by device type; the page includes, for example, F.H. Industrie CALCANAIL threaded cannulated screw (5 September 2026). MHRA says it publishes them for information only and a recipient must act on a notice from the manufacturer.
localIntel.quote: If you receive a field safety notice (FSN) from a manufacturer you must always act on it.
localIntel.use: Where a recall or correction on an orthopaedic product first appears publicly. Scan by manufacturer name each week.

localIntel.title: ODEP product ratings: hip, knee and other implants
localIntel.fact: ODEP's products page lists rated implant components with component name, material and a 'Next ODEP Review Due' field, searchable by supplier and filterable by rating. The site also has pages for Beyond Compliance implants, digital certificates and procurement. Ratings are not restated here; read the entry for the product concerned.
localIntel.quote: Next ODEP Review Due
localIntel.use: A surgeon or procurement lead will ask for an implant's ODEP rating. Check the product's entry and its review due date before a conversation.

localIntel.title: NHFD 2026 annual report, 'Mind the Gap', and live key performance indicators
localIntel.fact: The 2026 NHFD annual report, on 2025 data, was published 10 September 2026 and highlights continued variation in hip fracture care across hospitals. The key performance indicator page, annualised on 70,699 cases to the end of August 2026, shows: admission to specialist ward 10%; prompt orthogeriatric review 90%; prompt surgery 57%; NICE-compliant surgery 71%; promptly out of bed 82%; not delirious post-operatively 68%; return to original residence 75%; bone medication 62%.
localIntel.quote: NHFD Report 2026 (10 September 2026)
localIntel.use: National benchmarks for hip fracture care, relevant to trauma implants and orthogeriatric pathway conversations.

localIntel.title: Hospital Admitted Patient Care Activity 2025-26: procedure and provider tables
localIntel.fact: The 2025-26 publication covers 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 and records 22.6 million finished consultant episodes, up 71,455 (0.3%) on 2024-25. Downloads on the page include a procedures-and-interventions table, a provider table (hospital trusts) and a specialty table. Procedure counts are by operation code, so each code must be matched to a named procedure before a figure is quoted; this entry states no orthopaedic count.
localIntel.quote: In 2025-26 there were 22.6 million FCEs recorded.
localIntel.use: The source for national and trust procedure volumes by operation code once the codes are mapped.

localIntel.title: GIRFT surgical hub accreditation: 83 hubs by June 2026, 125 in operation
localIntel.fact: At cohort 12 (announced 1 June 2026) the total accredited since March 2023 was 83. GIRFT runs quarterly cohorts aiming to accredit all 125 hubs in operation in England. The scheme is run with the Royal College of Surgeons and supported by the Royal College of Anaesthetists. Hubs focus on high-volume, low-complexity surgery including trauma and orthopaedics (including spinal surgery). Cohort 12's hubs include the Essex and Suffolk Elective Orthopaedic Centre, Pontefract Hospital Elective Orthopaedic Centre and Hampshire Elective Orthopaedic Centre. Earlier cohort announcements are on the same site.
localIntel.quote: GIRFT is running quarterly cohorts to accredit all 125 hubs currently in operation across the NHS in England.
localIntel.use: Surgical hubs are where much elective orthopaedic volume is moving. This names accredited orthopaedic centres and the programme's target.
